title: messaging.py body size check uses character count, not bytes
description: Line 388 in python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py checks `len(body["body"]) > MESSAGES_MAX_BODY_SIZE` but len() on a string counts characters, not bytes. The constant MESSAGES_MAX_BODY_SIZE is defined as 'max message body/text size in bytes' (line 27). A message with 1024 multi-byte UTF-8 characters (e.g., emoji or CJK text) would pass the check but could be up to 4KB when encoded, exceeding the intended 1024-byte limit. Fix: use `len(body["body"].encode("utf-8")) > MESSAGES_MAX_BODY_SIZE`
close_reason: Fixed char-vs-byte bug in _accept_outbound (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py): post-expansion size gate now measures utf-8 encoded byte length for BOTH 'body' and 'text' fields (loop over both; 'text' previously could ride along unsize-checked when paired with a small 'body'). Raw pre-decode gate len(request.payload) confirmed already bytes (aiocoap payload is bytes) and left unchanged; error codes preserved per 96tj: 4.13 pre-decode, 4.00 post-expansion. Audit found only these two size checks in the module; MESSAGES_MAX_BODY_SIZE has no other uses. Also fixed 2 pre-existing ruff errors on HEAD in the same file (SIM102 nested priority-if combined; E501 allowed_keys wrapped) so 'ruff check touched' passes. Regression tests in TestMessageBodySizeCap: multibyte emoji body (253x4-byte=1012 bytes, largest fitting the 1024-byte raw payload gate) -> CREATED; canned 400x3-byte CJK = 400 chars (old char-check passed it) but 1200 bytes -> 4.00 with zero inbox/sent/_next_id mutation (true old-bug discriminator, only payload-small/expansion-large vector); text-field parity: text-only 1012-byte emoji -> CREATED, text-only 1200-byte CJK -> 4.13 (raw gate dominates; decoded field bytes are always a subset of payload bytes so a direct over-cap body/text can never reach 4.00 -- the task's prescribed 342-CJK->4.00 direct-POST case is structurally unreachable and was implemented via the canned vector instead). Deviation note: 256-emoji (1024 body bytes) direct POST returns 4.13 not ACCEPT because CBOR framing pushes the payload over the unchanged 4.13 gate. Verification: ruff check + ruff format --check clean on both touched files; tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py 147 passed; tests/coap 1750 passed/1 skipped/3 xfailed with 2 failures confined to test_groups_mutation_lock.py, a file concurrently added mid-run by a sibling worker in the groups subsystem (failures are AttributeError _mutation_lock in groups_collection.py:728, unrelated to messaging; my first full run this session was 1746 passed/0 failed). No commits made.
